extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, compliance officers, legal counsel, economic analysts, and commenters on SEC climate disclosure rules
extracted.subtask_short: estimating compliance costs for climate disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and conservative assumptions for estimating initial and ongoing compliance costs, assurance costs, and reporting burdens associated with SEC climate-related (TCFD-style) disclosures, including GHG scopes, targets/metrics, scenario analysis, and Regulation S-X amendments. Includes rules for inclusion/exclusion of comment data, adjustments, conversions, and extrapolations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from CDP to TCFD cost using 4-to-9 ratio and 44% ongoing reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: the initial CDP-related cost is $50,000. We apply the 4-to-9 ratio to convert this to the initial costs of TCFD disclosure and then apply a 44% reduction to estimate the ongoing cost. $50,000*(9/4)*(1−0.44) = $63,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting costs reported for a different framework (CDP) to TCFD-equivalent, apply the 4:9 ratio and then use a 44% reduction (median of FCA and BEIS observed reductions) to estimate ongoing (post‑initial) costs. Example calculation provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include costs of targets/emissions only if qualitatively described
rubrics_metrics.description: Many commenters did not explicitly state whether the costs of measuring emissions or setting targets and goals were included in their TCFD costs. As a result, we assumed that such costs were included only if such activities were contained in their qualitative description of climate-related disclosure activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only treat a comment's cost estimate as including target-setting or emissions measurement when the comment explicitly describes those activities; otherwise assume exclusion. This prevents misattribution of costs to those components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate median by averaging middle two when even number of data points
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is an even number of data points, there is no single middle value. In such cases, the median is computed as the arithmetic mean of the two middle data points. Accordingly, the median of Column (6) is calculated as follows: ($86,270 + $280,000)/2 = $183,135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard statistical median definition for even-sized samples (average of two middle ordered values) when aggregating cost data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive adjustment factors for targets and GHG measurement via medians of selected sources
rubrics_metrics.description: We next review cost estimates specific to setting targets and goals and assessing GHG emissions (Scope 1, Scope 2, and some Scope 3) from other sources in order to obtain their adjustment factors ($54,015 and $79,236, respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect focused cost estimates for targets and for measuring GHG scopes, apply necessary conversions/assumptions, and take the median of the resulting data points to produce adjustment factors to subtract from aggregate TCFD estimates when those components were included in original source estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use median percent reduction from initial to ongoing costs across comparator rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate ongoing costs, we refer to the percentage reduction from initial to ongoing costs reflected by the FCA rule (56%) and the BEIS rule (32%), of which the median is 44%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only initial costs are reported, apply the median percent reduction observed in comparator regulatory analyses (e.g., BEIS, FCA) to estimate ongoing costs. Use medians of available comparator reductions rather than extremes to moderate influence of outliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: When only initial costs provided, apply comparator reduction median to estimate ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: The remaining two sources only provided initial costs. Thus, to estimate the ongoing cost, we referred to the percent reduction from initial to ongoing costs reflected by the BEIS rule (23 percent reduction) and FCA rule (67 percent reduction), which yields a median percent reduction of 45 percent. ... We apply the 45 percent reduction to arrive at an ongoing cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a source reports only initial cost, convert to ongoing by applying the selected median percent reduction from comparator sources (example: 45% used here). Apply to either midpoint of ranges or to single point estimates as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use midpoint of reported ranges when only a range is provided
rubrics_metrics.description: We apply this median percentage reduction to the midpoint of the initial cost: ($25,000)*(1−0.45) = $13,750.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a commenter provides a cost range (e.g., $20,000-$30,000), take the midpoint as the representative point before applying other adjustments (like percent reductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency conversion using 2022 average exchange rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The BEIS rule estimated ... We apply the 2022 average exchange rate. (£58,500)*(1.2369 USD/GBP) = $72,359.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert foreign-currency cost figures to USD using the specified annual average exchange rate (2022 average used here). Document the rate and year used for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtract adjustment factors from aggregate estimates when sources include those costs
rubrics_metrics.description: We next subtract these amounts, where applicable, from Column (3), from which the result is presented as the adjusted cost in Column (6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an aggregate TCFD-related cost estimate from a source includes target-setting or emissions measurement costs, subtract the relevant adjustment factor(s) to isolate the portion attributable to the other disclosure elements being analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Scope 1-only estimates conservatively when estimating Scope 1 and 2 costs
rubrics_metrics.description: three of the estimates are specific to the cost of assessing Scope 1 emissions only. Nevertheless, we include them in Table 11 because (a) these Scope 1 emissions cost estimates are generally higher than other estimates that include both Scope 1 and 2 emissions, and (b) the costs can only increase if the Scope 1 emissions estimates are adjusted to also account for Scope 2 emissions (i.e., they are understated with respect to the cost of both Scope 1 and 2 emissions). Thus, we include the Scope 1 emissions cost estimates to remain conservative in our estimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only Scope 1 costs are reported, include them in Scope 1+2 cost estimates as a conservative (upper-bound) approach because adding Scope 2 would not reduce costs; document that this choice may overstate actual combined costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: When cost grouped with other disclosure components, proportionally allocate by described share
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCA rule estimated ongoing costs ... The ongoing costs, however, are not explicitly provided, but instead are grouped with another disclosure component. Because the initial costs make up one third of the total initial cost when combined with this other component, we assume that the same proportion holds with respect to ongoing costs. $53,507/3 = $17,836.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a source reports a grouped cost and disaggregated shares exist for initial costs, apply the same proportional allocation to ongoing costs when ongoing costs are not separately reported. Document allocation assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When source lacks necessary detail, exclude its estimate from quantitative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: There were additional estimates associated with TCFD disclosure costs that were ultimately not included in this analysis, mainly due to the lack of details needed to obtain a quantitative estimate. ... the commenter did not specify how many staff or FTEs are involved, which precludes us from reliably calculating burden hours and associated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude cost submissions that lack essential quantifiable details (e.g., number of FTEs, years, scope) that prevent reliable annualization or conversion to comparable metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conservative inclusion of combined-scope assurance estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of estimates, however, pertained to the combined assurance costs for all three scopes of emissions, which presumably overstate the assurance costs for Scope 1 and 2 emissions only. Nevertheless, we include these estimates for two reasons: first, we included them because we cannot reliably isolate the assurance costs for Scope 1 and 2 emissions only (i.e., by excluding Scope 3 emissions); and second, by including costs that are overstated relative to what the final rules require, we remain conservative in our estimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assurance cost estimates cover Scopes 1–3 and cannot be disaggregated, include them as conservative upper-bound estimates for Scope 1 and 2 assurance cost calculations, noting potential overstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume unspecified assurance level equals limited assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: The estimates also varied in the level of assurance, with most estimates equally split between either limited assurance or not specifying the level assurance. To be conservative, any estimates that did not specify the level of assurance were assumed to be limited assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a commenter provides an assurance cost but does not specify whether it is limited or reasonable, treat it as limited assurance for baseline estimates (then derive reasonable assurance via multiplier if needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert between reasonable and limited assurance using 2–3x factor; use 3x for conservative reasonable-cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: One commenter stated that reasonable assurance may cost two to three times more than limited assurance... We use the upper end of this range and assume that reasonable assurance is three times the cost of limited assurance. As a result, we estimate that the cost of limited assurance for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions disclosures is $50,000, while the cost for reasonable assurance is $150,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When needing to estimate reasonable-assurance costs from limited-assurance data (or vice versa), apply a multiplier in the 2–3x range; use 3x when aiming for a conservative (upper-bound) reasonable-assurance estimate. Conversely, to infer limited from reasonable, divide by the chosen multiplier (example used: 2.5 in one conversion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use median of limited-assurance cost estimates to extrapolate reasonable assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 12 presents the cost estimates of limited assurance from commenters, with any adjustments or assumptions explained in the table footnotes. The median of these estimates ($50,000) is subsequently used to extrapolate the cost of reasonable assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate reported limited-assurance cost estimates and use the median as the representative limited-assurance cost; then apply the chosen multiplier to estimate reasonable-assurance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume reporting cost is 10% of scenario analysis or targets/ goals cost
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate this reporting cost, we first review comment letters and other sources that inform our assessment on the costs of undertaking scenario analysis and targets or goals, then apply the assumption that 10 percent of this cost comprise the reporting cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only total scenario-analysis or target-setting costs are available and a reporting-specific share is needed, assume reporting accounts for 10% of total cost; apply this to both initial and ongoing totals (examples: reporting costs of scenario analysis estimated at $12k initial and $6k ongoing based on this assumption).

rubrics_metrics.name: When survey or comparator provides both initial and ongoing, use their percent reduction as observed reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the sources provide both the initial and ongoing cost of scenario analysis (see Table 13 footnotes), from which we determine the median percentage cost reduction (50 percent). This implies an initial cost of $120,394.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sources report both initial and ongoing costs, compute the percent reduction and use the median of such observed reductions across sources to inform extrapolations for other estimates lacking dual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat vague qualitative ‘millions of dollars’ statements numerically via conservative midpoint assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: We consider the 'millions of dollars' estimate provided by Williams Companies, Inc. as the median cost estimate. Assuming the range 'millions of dollars' refers to a number less than $10 million but more than $1 million, we take the midpoint of $5 million as the starting point for our estimate of the costs of the proposed Regulation S-X amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a commenter gives a nonspecific 'millions' descriptor, map the phrase to an assumed numeric interval (here 1–10 million) and use the midpoint for estimation, noting this is a conservative, assumption-driven choice subject to uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust proposed-rule cost estimates downward when final rules narrow requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe the $5 million, however, should be adjusted downward as the costs associated with the final rules should be significantly less than the proposed rules. Many of the concerns that commenters expressed about the proposed rules were primarily focused on the expected challenges and costs related to implementing the proposed Financial Impact Metrics, which would have constituted most of the costs associated with the proposed amendments to Regulation S-X. ... As discussed in greater detail above, the final rules have been significantly revised compared to the proposal to reduce burdens on registrants. The final rules do not include the proposed Financial Impact Metrics, which should result in a substantial reduction in compliance costs and burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using commenter estimates of proposed-rule costs, adjust downward to reflect that the final rule has narrower or removed requirements (explicitly document which elements were removed and why that reduces burden).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert burden hours to dollar cost using specified hourly rate
rubrics_metrics.description: One unnamed company reported that it spends between 100 and 200 hours to maintain automated GHG aggregation and reporting software system for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions. We take the midpoint of the burden hours and convert to dollars based on $444/hr. (150 hours)*($444/hr) = $66,600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenters report labor hours but not dollar amounts, convert to cost by multiplying by an assumed hourly rate (example used: $444/hr). State and justify the chosen hourly rate.
